about.title: About Lingora
about.whatBody: Lingora helps a Deaf signer and a hearing person communicate. Experimental recognition compares one sign at a time with labeled video examples. The signer checks the text before it is spoken, and the hearing person can reply by speech or typing.
about.signsNote: This list shows signs with loaded examples, not a verified general-purpose vocabulary. Performance on new signers has not been established.
about.notFor.cta: In these situations, ask for a human interpreter.
about.limit1: Only signs with loaded video examples can be matched. It cannot translate continuous signing.
about.limit2: It can be wrong. You confirm every sign and every sentence before anything is read aloud.
about.limit3: It does not translate text into signs.
about.limit4: Uzbek speech needs a configured speech service or a compatible installed voice. Typing remains available.
about.privacyBody: Camera video and imported lesson videos are processed on this device. Conversation text stays in this session in local mode. Microphone audio is sent to a speech provider when speech recognition is used. Speech synthesis may send the confirmed text to that provider. Video examples stay in memory unless you explicitly export them.

welcome.lead: Lingora helps a Deaf signer and a hearing person talk to each other, in Uzbek, Russian and English.
welcome.how1: The signer presses Sign now and signs. Lingora shows what it recognised.
welcome.how2: The signer confirms. Lingora writes a sentence and reads it aloud.
welcome.how3: The hearing person types or speaks. The reply appears in large, simple text.
welcome.guestNote: As a guest nothing is saved.
welcome.limits: Lingora is a conversation aid and can be wrong. Do not use it for medical, legal or emergency situations. Ask for a human interpreter instead.
